It agrees with Apollonius. But about Cleite, Deiiochus (fg 8 M. II 18) says that she died of grief. Apollonius records that Cyzicus was killed childless, but Neanthes (see above) says that he had a son of the same name.
1 Δηίοχος with the letter λ deleted in V : Διίοχος in P : Δηίλοχος in L; 3 Νεάνθης C. Mueller FHG III 11 : Εὐάνθης; ἑαυτῷ at the end added in P
8 Parth. Narr. am. 28

7 Νεάνθης Marquardt Cyzicus 1836, 168 n. 1 : Εὐάνθης; 8 Δηίοχος W : Διίοχος in P : Δηίλοχος in L and V; 9 ἐκ Fr. : ἡ L. W indicated a lacuna. P, whom Jacoby follows, filled the whole passage thus: καὶ Δ. δὲ καὶ Εὐ. ἀπάγξασθαί φασιν αὐτήν, καὶ ἐκ τῶν δακρύων αὐτῆς κρήνην γενέσθαι, κληθεῖσαν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτῆς Κλείτην.

14 sch. β 355; Apoll. Lex. Hom. 114, 9 B.; Hesych. μυληφάτου; Et. Or. 98, 19; Et. M. 594, 42; Eust. 868, 39. 1445, 57. 1450, 18

18 Et. Gen. (B) χύτλα: as in II 926. χύτλα properly are oils mixed with water, but by misuse also the offerings to the dead. Callimachus (fg 479 Schn.): ‘χύτλων ἀντιασάντων (ἀντιάσαντες Schneider)’, ἔντομα μήλων are the castrated ones, since they especially sacrificed these to the dead as being barren to those who are themselves barren (from ἔντομα repeated from the gloss ἔντομα, which was ascribed to v. 587). cf. W 77; sch. ζ 80; Hesych.; Suid. χύτλα

19 Et. Gen. (AB) πέλανος: as in I 1077. They are certain cakes. The Attics call πέλανος everything that is congealed, as Euripides used the word for the foam congealed around the teeth, as (Orest. 220):
but they call everything congealed thus. But the
